name: Mount Rainier Skyline Trail
unique: A 14,410-foot glaciated volcano with wildflower meadows at 6,000 feet, and a loop trail that puts Rainier, the Tatoosh Range and a waterfall in one frame.
buzz: The wildflowers in late July are legendary; the trail is crowded and the altitude is real. Start early for parking.

name: Hoh Rainforest
unique: A temperate rainforest of moss-draped maples and Sitka spruce, with the Hall of Mosses and a river the color of green glass.
buzz: People whisper in the Hall of Mosses; it is genuinely otherworldly. Rain is likely and part of the experience.

name: North Cascades
unique: Jagged peaks, turquoise glacial lakes and more glaciers than any other park in the lower 48, with a highway that crosses three dams and a pass.
buzz: People call it the American Alps and note how empty it is; the trails are steep and the weather changes fast.

name: DirtFish Rally School
unique: Rally driving school on a gravel and forest stage, with instructors who teach you to slide a car sideways on purpose and a fleet of prepared Subarus.
buzz: The half day course is enough to be humbling and addictive; the forest setting is beautiful in the rain. Book months ahead.

name: San Juan Islands Orca Kayak
customer: Wildlife people, couples, families with teens
unique: Paddle the Salish Sea among the San Juan islands, with resident orcas, humpbacks, porpoises and bald eagles, and no guarantee of any of them.
buzz: Guides are excellent on whale-watch rules; the kayak is quieter and closer than a boat. Sightings are luck, so book two days.

name: Hurricane Ridge
unique: A road that climbs to 5,242 feet in Olympic National Park for a view of the Bailey Range and the Strait of Juan de Fuca, with trails into alpine meadows.
buzz: The view on a clear day is the best drive in the park and the winter snowshoe is the local secret; check the road report, it closes for weather.

name: Lake Chelan and Stehekin
company: National Park Service and Lady of the Lake
unique: A 55 mile glacial lake that runs into the North Cascades, with a ferry to Stehekin, a roadless valley at the far end with a bakery and a waterfall.
buzz: The ferry ride up the lake is the day and Stehekin is the reward; the boat takes four hours each way, so many people stay overnight.

name: Mount St. Helens
unique: The volcano that blew its top in 1980, with a crater, a lava dome, a buried forest and a visitor center that shows the blast minute by minute.
buzz: The Johnston Ridge view is extraordinary on a clear day; clouds can erase everything. Check the webcam before driving.

name: Museum of Flight
unique: A collection that includes a Concorde, the first Boeing 747 and a SR-71 Blackbird, with a walk through the original Red Barn where Boeing built its first planes.
buzz: The SR-71 and the 747 are the two planes people photograph and the Red Barn is the history; the museum is on Boeing Field and the tower tour is extra.

name: North Cascades Highway
unique: The most scenic mountain pass in the state, crossing 5,477 feet through the North Cascades with trailheads to turquoise lakes and glaciers at every pullout.
buzz: The drive from Marblemount to Winthrop is the day and the Diablo Lake overlook is the photograph; the road closes with snow from November to April.

name: Pike Place Market
unique: A century old public market on a bluff above the sound: fish throwing, the original Starbucks, a gum wall and a maze of levels that rewards wandering.
buzz: Go at 8am before the crowds and eat at a counter; the fish throw is a photo op, the produce is the real thing.

name: Palouse
unique: Rolling loess hills planted in wheat, lentils and canola, forming green and gold waves that look like a painting from the ridge roads.
buzz: Photographers plan around harvest and sunrise; the back roads are gravel and the towns are tiny. Steptoe Butte is the viewpoint.

name: Boeing Future of Flight
unique: The tour of the Everett factory, the largest building by volume in the world, where 747s, 777s and 787s are assembled on catwalks above the floor.
buzz: The factory floor is the thing people cannot get over and the tour needs booking; the gallery has a 787 dreamliner you can walk through.

name: Chihuly Garden and Glass
unique: A glasshouse and garden of Dale Chihuly's work at the foot of the Space Needle, with a ceiling of glass flowers and towers that light up at night.
buzz: The glasshouse and the garden at dusk are the two visits; the combo ticket with the Space Needle saves money and the exhibits are indoors on rainy days.

name: Deception Pass
unique: A bridge 180 feet above a churning tidal channel between two islands, with cliffs, old growth forest and sea lions below.
buzz: The bridge walk is free and thrilling; the currents are dangerous for swimming. Sunset from the bridge is the shot.

name: Cape Flattery
unique: The northwestern tip of the contiguous United States, where a boardwalk leads to sea caves and a view of Tatoosh Island and the open Pacific.
buzz: The boardwalk and the sea stacks are the photograph and the drive is remote; a Makah recreation permit is required and the trail can be muddy.

name: Lake Quinault
unique: A rain forest lake ringed by the largest trees in the state, with a loop trail through old growth spruce and a 1926 lodge on the shore.
buzz: The loop drive and the Rain Forest Nature Trail are the easy version and the Enchanted Valley trail is the epic; it rains most of the year.

name: Mount Baker
unique: A 10,781 foot volcano with the world record for snowfall, a road to Artist Point at 5,100 feet and trails into the Heather Meadows.
buzz: Artist Point in July and August is the view of Shuksan and the mountain and the snow lingers into summer; the road is closed in winter below the lodge.

name: Seattle Glassblowing Studio
unique: A hot shop near the waterfront where you can blow a float or a tumbler in a class, or watch a demo and buy work from local artists.
buzz: The make your own class is the draw and the staff are good with nervous beginners; pieces ship if you are traveling.

name: Dungeness Spit
unique: The longest natural sand spit in the country, five and a half miles into the Strait of Juan de Fuca, with a lighthouse at the end and a protected estuary behind it.
buzz: The walk to the lighthouse takes most of a day and most people turn around at the first mile; the estuary is closed in winter for birds.

name: LeMay America's Car Museum
unique: A silver wave shaped building above Interstate 5 holding 300 cars from the LeMay collection, including a 1906 Cadillac and a Tucker, with a driving simulator.
buzz: Car people say the collection is one of the best in the country and the building is the landmark; the rotating exhibits keep it fresh.

name: Museum of Glass
unique: A museum with a working hot shop where you can watch a team gather and blow glass, and a cone of steel and glass on the Thea Foss waterway.
buzz: The hot shop demonstrations are the reason to come and the Chihuly bridge of glass outside is free; the museum is small enough for two hours.

name: Walla Walla Wine Tasting
unique: More than 120 wineries in a valley that produces some of the state's best syrah, with a walkable downtown of tasting rooms and a sweet onion festival in June.
buzz: Wine people rate the syrah with the best in the country and the downtown tasting rooms make a car unnecessary; spring and fall are the best weather.

name: Ye Olde Curiosity Shop
unique: A waterfront shop of mummies, shrunken heads and carved totems that has been collecting oddities since 1899, with a real mermaid and a two headed calf.
buzz: It is free to wander and deeply weird; the mummy is the main attraction. A good stop before the ferry.

name: Discovery Park
unique: Five hundred and thirty four acres of forest, meadow and sea cliffs on the old Fort Lawton, with a lighthouse and a beach on Puget Sound.
buzz: The loop trail to the lighthouse is the walk and the meadow is the birding; the park is big and the beach is a steep climb back.

name: Icicle Gorge
unique: A loop trail along the Icicle River through a granite gorge, with a footbridge over the water and a view up to the Stuart Range.
buzz: The loop is four miles of easy walking and the bridge is the photograph; the trailhead is a rough road and the parking is limited.

name: Lady Washington
unique: A replica of the first American ship to round Cape Horn, sailing from Grays Harbor with passengers hauling lines and standing watch on the deck.
buzz: The crew lets passengers help sail and the ship appears in films; the sailings sell out in summer and the dock is in Aberdeen.

name: Leavenworth
unique: A failing logging town remade itself as a Bavarian village, with nutcrackers, bratwurst, accordion music and the Cascades as a backdrop.
buzz: It is kitsch executed with real commitment; Oktoberfest is a mob and the Christmas lights are genuinely charming.

name: Riverfront Park
unique: A park built for the 1974 world's fair on the Spokane River, with a gondola over the falls, a 1909 carousel and a giant red wagon you can climb on.
buzz: The falls and the wagon are the photographs and the gondola is the ride; the park is free and the carousel is a dollar or two.

name: Yakima Valley Wine Country
unique: The oldest wine region in the state, with 90 wineries and vineyards in a desert valley below the Rattlesnake Hills, where the fruit gets ripe and the tasting rooms are cheap.
buzz: Wine people say the reds are the value and the tasting rooms are informal; book a driver, the valley is long and the roads are two lane.

name: Bale Breaker Brewing
unique: A brewery built in the middle of a hop field that the family has farmed for four generations, with a taproom that looks out over the bines.
buzz: The fresh hop beers in September are the reason beer people make the drive and the outdoor seating is the setting; the taproom is closed early on weekdays.

name: Jetty Island
unique: A man made island of sand and dune grass in Puget Sound, reached by a free ferry, with shallow warm water and a long empty beach.
buzz: The shallow water is warm by Puget Sound standards and the ferry is free; the island is only open in summer and the wind is constant.

name: Manito Park
unique: Ninety acres with a formal Duncan garden, a Japanese garden, a rose hill and a greenhouse conservatory, all free in the middle of the city.
buzz: The Japanese garden and the Duncan garden are the two stops and the park is free; the greenhouse is the winter visit.

name: Point Defiance Zoo and Aquarium
unique: A zoo and aquarium in a 760 acre park on Puget Sound, with polar bears, walruses and a Pacific seas aquarium, plus a ferry to the park.
buzz: The walruses and the aquarium are the family draw and the park around it has trails and a beach; the hill is steep and the zoo is compact.

name: Toppenish Murals
unique: More than 70 murals painted on downtown walls telling the history of the Yakama Nation and the railroad town, best seen by horse drawn wagon.
buzz: The wagon tour in summer is the way to see them and the murals are genuinely good; the town is small and the drive from Yakima is 30 minutes.

name: Whitman Mission
unique: The site of the 1847 mission where the Whitmans were killed, with the foundation of the mission house, a wagon ruts trail and a museum on the Cayuse War.
buzz: The ranger talks tell the story from both sides and the wagon ruts are the real thing; it is free and the walk is flat.

name: Fairhaven Historic District
unique: A brick Victorian district on Bellingham Bay built on a gold rush that never happened, with a village green, a bookstore and a ferry to the San Juan Islands.
buzz: The bookshop and the waterfront trail are the local stops and the Alaska ferry terminal is at the bottom of the hill; the district is small and walkable.

name: Fort Walla Walla Museum
unique: A pioneer village of 17 original buildings, a horse era machinery hall and a military museum on the old fort grounds.
buzz: The pioneer village is the family draw and the machinery hall is the surprise; the living history weekends bring it alive.

name: Mukilteo Lighthouse
unique: A 1906 lighthouse on a point above the ferry landing, with a keeper's house, a beach and a view of Whidbey Island across the sound.
buzz: The lighthouse and the ferry crossing are the photograph and the beach is a good picnic; the tour is weekends only.

name: Northwest Museum of Arts and Culture
company: Northwest Museum of Arts and Culture
unique: A museum in a 1916 mansion with regional Native artifacts, a Campbell House next door and a gallery of western art, run by the historical society.
buzz: The Campbell House and the Native collection are the reasons to come; the museum is small and the mansion is a step back into 1898.

name: Slidewaters
unique: A water park above Lake Chelan with slides built into the hillside and a view of the lake from the lazy river, in a town that gets 300 days of sun.
buzz: The view from the slides is the reason people drive from Seattle and the lines are short on weekdays; the park is small.

name: Westport Light
unique: A 1898 lighthouse at the end of a jetty on the Pacific, with a boardwalk over the dunes and a view of Grays Harbor and the open ocean.
buzz: The boardwalk and the jetty are the walk and the beach is wide and windy; the town is the base for charter fishing.
